chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
Whoever recites Iqra' bismi rabbika, then when he completes it, let him perform sajdah; then when he rises, let him recite Fatihat al-Kitab and perform ruku'.

He said: If you are tried with an Imam who does not perform sajdah, then indication by gesture and ruku' will suffice you. And do not recite it in the obligatory prayer; recite it in the supererogatory prayer.

key_terms.اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ: the opening phrase of Surah al-'Alaq, the surah being discussed
key_terms.الْإِيمَاءُ: gesturing as a substitute when full sajdah cannot be performed
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Surah al-Fatihah, to be recited after rising
key_terms.فَلْيَسْجُدْ: let him perform the obligatory sajdah upon finishing the surah

ai.seo_question: Can Surah al-'Alaq be recited in obligatory prayer if it contains a verse of sajdah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about reciting a surah of the obligatory sajdah, specifically Surah al-'Alaq, in prayer. It instructs that sajdah must be performed upon completing it, explains what to do when praying behind an Imam who does not perform the sajdah, and prohibits reciting it in the obligatory prayer while allowing it in supererogatory prayer.
